title: Okanin attenuates ovariectomy-induced bone loss in mice model through inhibition of IKKbeta-mediated NF-kappaB p65 phosphorylation.
authors: Shi, Kai; Wang, Ying-Jian; Wang, Shaoming; Guan, Zhenhong; Li, Man; Zhao, Ya-Nan; Sun, Wan-Chun
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究黄酮类化合物okanin通过抑制IKKbeta/NF-kappaB信号通路减轻骨质疏松小鼠骨丢失，属于纯药理学与骨代谢研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Excessive activation of osteoclasts can lead to excessive bone resorption, thereby causing bone loss diseases. Okanin, a flavonoid derived from Coreopsis tinctoria, has been reported to possess antibacterial, anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, and has therapeutic effects on cerebral ischemia. Although okanin is known for other biological activities, its role in bone metabolism has not been clearly elucidated before. PURPOSE: In the present study, we evaluated the effects of okanin on osteoclast formation and function through in vitro assays, and further assessed its capacity to mitigate bone loss in a murine model of ovariectomy (OVX)-induced osteoporosis in vivo. STUDY DESIGN: We employed a combination of in vitro cell-based assays and an in vivo ovariectomy (OVX)-induced osteoporosis mouse model to systematically assess okanin's bone-protective effects and underlying mechanisms. METHODS: In vitro, bone marrow macrophages (BMMs) were treated with okanin (1.25-20 muM) during RANKL-induced osteoclast differentiation. Key endpoints included TRAP-positive multinucleated cell formation, F-actin ring integrity, resorption pit activity, and expression of osteoclastogenic markers (c-Fos, NFATc1) and signaling molecules (IKKbeta, NF-kappaB p65). In silico molecular docking analyzed okanin's interaction with IKKalpha/beta. In vivo, OVX mice were administered okanin (2 or 10 mg/kg, i.p.) for 8 weeks, followed by micro-CT, histological, and TRAP staining analyses of femurs to assess bone microarchitecture and osteoclast activity. RESULTS: In vitro, okanin dose-dependently inhibited RANKL-induced osteoclast differentiation and disrupted F-actin ring formation without cytotoxicity. It downregulated c-Fos, NFATc1, and their target genes (TRAP, MMP-9, Atp6v0d2), while selectively suppressing IKKbeta phosphorylation and NF-kappaB p65 activation (without affecting MAPK pathways or IKKalpha). Okanin also blunted RANKL-induced Blimp1 upregulation and preserved NFATc1 inhibitors (Bcl6, MafB, IRF8). In vivo, okanin dose-dependently preserved trabecular bone architecture in OVX mice, improving bone volume fraction (BV/TV), trabecular number (Tb.N), and thickness (Tb.Th), while reducing osteoclast numbers. CONCLUSION: In conclusion, these findings establish okanin as a novel bone-protective agent that inhibits osteoclastogenesis through a distinct mechanism involving selective IKKbeta/NF-kappaB inhibition, thereby attenuating OVX-induced bone loss. This specificity distinguishes it from other compounds and highlights its promise as a lead candidate for development as a functional food supplement or therapeutic agent for osteoporosis.
abstract_zh: 背景：破骨细胞的过度活化可导致骨吸收过度，从而引发骨丢失疾病。Okanin是一种源自金鸡菊（Coreopsis tinctoria）的黄酮类化合物，已有报道称其具有抗菌、抗炎和抗氧化活性，并对脑缺血具有治疗作用。尽管okanin已知具有其他生物活性，但其在骨代谢中的作用此前尚未被明确阐明。目的：在本研究中，我们通过体外实验评估了okanin对破骨细胞形成和功能的影响，并进一步评估其在体内卵巢切除（OVX）诱导的骨质疏松小鼠模型中减轻骨丢失的能力。研究设计：我们采用体外细胞实验与体内卵巢切除（OVX）诱导的骨质疏松小鼠模型相结合的方法，系统评估okanin的骨保护作用及其潜在机制。方法：体外实验中，在RANKL诱导的破骨细胞分化期间，用okanin（1.25-20 μM）处理骨髓巨噬细胞（BMMs）。关键终点包括TRAP阳性多核细胞形成、F-actin环完整性、骨吸收坑活性，以及破骨细胞生成标志物（c-Fos、NFATc1）和信号分子（IKKβ、NF-κB p65）的表达。通过计算机分子对接分析okanin与IKKα/β的相互作用。体内实验中，OVX小鼠接受okanin（2或10 mg/kg，腹腔注射）治疗8周，随后通过micro-CT、组织学和TRAP染色分析股骨，以评估骨微结构和破骨细胞活性。结果：体外实验中，okanin剂量依赖性地抑制RANKL诱导的破骨细胞分化，并破坏F-actin环形成，且无细胞毒性。它下调c-Fos、NFATc1及其靶基因（TRAP、MMP-9、Atp6v0d2）的表达，同时选择性抑制IKKβ磷酸化和NF-κB p65激活（不影响MAPK通路或IKKα）。Okanin还减弱了RANKL诱导的Blimp1上调，并保留了NFATc1抑制剂（Bcl6、MafB、IRF8）。体内实验中，okanin剂量依赖性地保留OVX小鼠的小梁骨结构，改善骨体积分数（BV/TV）、小梁数量（Tb.N）和厚度（Tb.Th），同时减少破骨细胞数量。结论：总之，这些发现确立了okanin作为一种新型骨保护剂，通过涉及选择性IKKβ/NF-κB抑制的独特机制抑制破骨细胞生成，从而减轻OVX诱导的骨丢失。这种特异性使其区别于其他化合物，并凸显其作为开发骨质疏松症功能性食品补充剂或治疗药物的先导候选物的潜力。
